audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Bildad's first speech: accusation of wind-words, traditional retribution theology, appeal to ancestors, papyrus/reed metaphor, forgotten-God claim, and restoration promise. Marked as Bildad's speech, not final theology.

verses.restored: Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:

familiar.text: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,

verses.restored: How long will you speak these things, and the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?

familiar.text: How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind?

verses.restored: Does the Divine twist justice? Does Shaddai twist righteousness?

familiar.text: Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?

verses.restored: If your children sinned against him, he sent them into the hand of their transgression.

familiar.text: If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression;

verses.restored: If you would seek the Divine and plead for favor from Shaddai,

familiar.text: If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;

verses.restored: if you are pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you and restore your righteous dwelling.

familiar.text: If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.

verses.restored: Though your beginning was small, your latter end would grow very great.

familiar.text: Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.

verses.restored: For ask, please, the former generation, and establish yourself by the search of their fathers.

familiar.text: For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:

verses.restored: For we are yesterday and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.

familiar.text: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:)

verses.restored: Will they not teach you, speak to you, and bring words out from their heart?

familiar.text: Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?

verses.restored: Can papyrus grow where there is no marsh? Can reeds grow without water?

familiar.text: Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water?

verses.restored: While still in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other grass.

familiar.text: Whilst it is yet in his greenness, and not cut down, it withereth before any other herb.

verses.restored: So are the paths of all who forget the Divine; the hope of the godless shall perish.

familiar.text: So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite’s hope shall perish:

verses.restored: His confidence is cut off, and his trust is a spider’s house.

familiar.text: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spider’s web.

verses.restored: He leans on his house, but it does not stand; he holds fast to it, but it does not endure.

familiar.text: He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.

verses.restored: He is fresh before the sun, and his shoot goes out over his garden.

familiar.text: He is green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.

verses.restored: His roots wrap around the stone heap; he sees the house of stones.

familiar.text: His roots are wrapped about the heap, and seeth the place of stones.

verses.restored: If he is swallowed from his place, it will deny him, saying, I have not seen you.

familiar.text: If he destroy him from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee.

verses.restored: Look, this is the joy of his way, and from the dust others will sprout.

familiar.text: Behold, this is the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.

verses.restored: Look, the Divine will not reject a whole person, nor will he grasp the hand of evildoers.

familiar.text: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers:

verses.restored: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouting.

familiar.text: Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing.

verses.restored: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.

familiar.text: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought.
